architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 is interpretable as a dual-axis thermal-hold uncertainty probe and may be promoted to a performance-mitigation test only if its formulation and process state are verifiable.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Before physical adjudication, verify AC1920 and TK100 identities, reactive-group densities, functionality, mass basis, and recalculated NCO:OH; predeclare a numerical processable 120 C initial-viscosity interval; run matched unmodified E2-like controls and at least duplicate, preferably triplicate, realizations with documented process history; then measure 120 C viscosity at 15, 60, and 90 min and report SI15-60 and SI15-90. Promotion to a performance claim requires reproducible, processable results with both SI values lower than the E5 reference values of 0.515 and 0.931 under the predeclared replicate-level uncertainty and effect-size rule.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Do not promote the candidate if modifier stoichiometry or processability cannot be verified, if required process history is undocumented, if replicate spread prevents the predeclared comparison, if either SI is not reproducibly reduced relative to E5, or if apparent improvement occurs only through a nonprocessable initial-viscosity shift.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Temperature sweep 80-130 C; thermal hold at 120 C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min; SI calculated for 15-60 and 15-90 min.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Full dual-axis coverage and stronger acrylic-region support than S1C41, but higher total modifier burden and greater departure from the characterized E2 chemistry; retain as a subsequent robustness comparison.
Lower-burden full-coverage boundary probe, but both modifier levels have weaker support and a null result would be difficult to distinguish from insufficient intervention.
Useful matched no-intervention control, but it zeroes both independently supported axes and therefore cannot serve as the primary performance-mitigation experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The failure mode is thermal-hold instability, demonstrated locally by E5 drift of SI15-60=0.515 and SI15-90=0.931 versus E1 values of 0.095 and 0.168. The declared intent is performance mitigation, so independently supported acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes must both remain active; removing either axis would convert the experiment into a partial-coverage mechanistic control. Local experiments establish that hold drift is distinct from static temperature dependence, that 120 C is within measured support, and that E2 has substantial realization/state variability. The state-aware rheology analysis supplies the rule that a 120 C anchor can calibrate viscosity scale within the local chemistry family, but it does not predict hold stability. Curated PUR literature supports the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like formulation family and broad regions, including a repeated minor-resin region near 5 wt%, but does not predict the local result or establish a molecular mechanism. S1C41 is therefore retained as the specified dual-axis uncertainty probe rather than accepted as a definitive performance candidate. The Skeptic objection is resolved by explicitly treating the combined result as a performance screen with no axis attribution and by requiring a later axis-specific or boundary comparison if attribution is needed. The Robustness-Adjudicator objection is resolved by making verified modifier specifications, stoichiometric recalculation, matched process controls, a numerical processability interval, and a quantitative replicate rule gating conditions for proceeding. The minimum-sufficient-intervention argument is not used to claim that 15/5 is sufficient; it only favors S1C41 over the higher-burden S1C46 among otherwise comparable full-coverage candidates after the uncertainty gate is satisfied. This decision identifies an evidence-supported formulation region, not an exact-property prediction.

evidence_coverage.note: Dual-axis coverage is supported directionally; acrylic evidence at 15 wt% is partly noncommensurate, and combined-axis benefit is unverified.

extrapolation.note: S1C41 lies within the constructed acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like candidate bounds, but the combined local hold response remains unmeasured.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required canonical bridge before candidate ranking. It will confirm the formulation-only versus state-aware structure, whether state calibration materially improves the master curve, the local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, and the specific measurement implications for selecting a hold-stability intervention.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective is established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, the E2 reactive-core anchor, the independently supported acrylic and tackifier axes, and the historical/claim boundary before comparing candidate points.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Obtain deterministic local stability descriptors for the lower-drift original reference so candidate adjudication can compare against an established stable behavior over the same measured 120 C window.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Obtain deterministic descriptors for the established high-drift original reference and retain the failure baseline without using any held-out formulation or outcome.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify realization/process-state risk around the reactive-core anchor before treating any candidate viscosity level or temperature response as a reproducible material property.

action_requests.name: get_temperature_support
action_requests.reason: Confirm the measured temperature domain for choosing an in-support viscosity anchor and avoid extrapolating the candidate decision outside the 80–130 C local support.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Retrieve transparent composition summaries for the measured reactive-core reference so modifier-axis changes can be evaluated without conflating chemistry with process state or violating stoichiometric constraints.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: thermal-hold SI from 15 to 60 min and from 15 to 90 min at an in-support temperature
absolute viscosity level at the selected anchor temperature
temperature-response slope or state-aware temperature-sensitivity coordinate within measured support
retention of the E2 reactive-core and stoichiometric feasibility
acrylic-like modifier fraction within the bounded candidate lattice
minor tackifier-like modifier fraction within the bounded candidate lattice
compatibility of the combined modifier loading with melt processability
distance from directly measured local chemistry and degree of extrapolation
counterfactual_checks: Would the proposed candidate still be preferred if its nominal viscosity were matched to the E2 anchor but its hold SI were not improved?
Would the decision change if the observed viscosity shift were attributed to process-state realization rather than modifier chemistry?
Does a modifier intervention improve hold stability relative to E5 without merely moving the material outside the measured viscosity or temperature domain?
Would an acrylic-only, tackifier-only, and combined intervention have materially different decision value under performance-mitigation objectives?
Does the candidate remain feasible if the most conservative interpretation of the external 15–25 wt% acrylic and below-about-10 wt% tackifier evidence is used?
Would the candidate conclusion survive exclusion of the noncommensurate literature viscosity values and reliance only on local rheology plus directional chemistry evidence?
Does the candidate reduce both 15–60 and 15–90 min drift, rather than improving only one hold interval?
If repeatability uncertainty is penalized, does the candidate still dominate a lower-risk reactive-core-preserving alternative?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result experiment point that mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving a measurable, processable viscosity level and distinguishing chemistry intervention from realization/process-state noise.
design_implications: Prioritize reduction of hot-hold drift rather than optimization of a single nominal viscosity value.
Evaluate candidate performance at an anchor temperature inside measured support, preferably 120 C if the local hold comparison is retained.
Measure the complete local hold window, including at least 15, 60, and 90 min, because thermal stability is time-dependent.
Keep the E2 reactive-core anchor explicit and vary only evidence-supported modifier axes within the constructed candidate lattice.

A multi-component intervention is admissible in performance_mitigation mode because acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes are independently supported; it should remain within the preconstructed 0–30 wt% acrylic and 0–10 wt% tackifier bounds.
Do not convert external 15%, 20%, or 25% acrylic values, or the approximately 10% tackifier guidance, into an exact total-formulation optimum.
Treat any candidate viscosity comparison as conditional on realization/process state because E2 repeatability is poor.
Preserve stoichiometric, process-history, and measurement-unit uncertainty; rheology alone cannot establish a molecular mechanism.
material_regularities_to_use: Temperature sweeps are monotonic decreasing with temperature over the measured 80–130 C support.

Temperature-response curves are well described by descriptive Andrade fits, but run-to-run level differences are large for E2, with CV approximately 0.46–0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8–3.6.
Thermal-hold behavior is a distinct response from nominal temperature dependence and must be measured directly rather than inferred from a temperature-sweep viscosity.
The original E1 and E5 hold trajectories establish a local stability contrast at 120 C over the measured 15–90 min window.
The local E2 formulation is the reactive-core anchor; candidate modifier changes should not be interpreted as changing the reactive core unless explicitly specified.
External evidence supports acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes as chemically plausible directions, but does not identify an exact local optimum or establish the local mechanism.

Acrylic evidence includes approximate 15–25 wt% analogue levels and comparative low-OH versus higher-OH stability behavior; these are directional or noncommensurate because chemistry, process history, and hold windows differ.
Tackifier evidence supports a minor modifier axis below about 10 wt% as a conservative extrapolation boundary, not as an exact formulation target.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is the established failure mode: the original E5 reference shows large viscosity growth at 120 C (SI 0.515 from 15 to 60 min and 0.931 from 15 to 90 min), whereas E1 is substantially more stable (SI 0.095 and 0.168). Nominal temperature-sweep measurements also show large E2 run spread, so process-state and realization uncertainty must not be conflated with viscosity or thermal response.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over the local measured range, 80–130 C, with a declared anchor temperature inside that range
Thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at the anchor temperature at minimum 15, 60, and 90 min
At least duplicate, preferably triplicate, realizations to quantify repeatability and process-state spread
Exact formulation masses, reactive-core stoichiometric quantities, modifier identities, and modifier fractions
Documented thermal and mixing history before rheology measurement
Viscosity units and measurement conditions preserved without unit conversion when unavailable
A comparison to the E1/E5 local hold baselines and to the pre-result candidate objective
uncertainty_triggers: State-aware summary does not show a reproducible state shift or one-point calibration benefit.
Candidate hold data are outside the measured 120 C or 15–90 min domain.
Large run spread remains comparable to the E2 CV and max/min ratios.
A viscosity decrease or increase is observed without a corresponding hold-stability interpretation.
Modifier identity, functionality, molecular weight, or reactive-group density differs from the analogue evidence in an uncontrolled way.
Combined acrylic and tackifier loading exceeds the bounded candidate-space rules.
Stoichiometric balance or reactive-core identity is not preserved.
A candidate appears stable only because its initial viscosity is substantially different or outside the processable range.
External analogue percentages are treated as exact optima rather than directional or conservative evidence.
Any inference would require the blinded held-out formulation or its outcome.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates thermal-hold instability rather than merely changing nominal viscosity.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across matched duplicate or triplicate realizations, both SI15-60 and SI15-90 must be lower than the E5 reference values of 0.515 and 0.931, respectively, with the direction retained after accounting for realization spread; the initial 120 C viscosity must remain within the predeclared processable range and the result must be interpretable relative to E1 and E5.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure is indicated by no reproducible reduction in either hold interval, improvement only through a substantially shifted or nonprocessable initial viscosity, run-to-run spread comparable to the E2 realization spread, or undocumented state/stoichiometric differences that prevent attribution.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C, 15-90 min, with SI calculated for 15-60 and 15-90 min.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: At 120 C, measure the complete thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 15, 60, and 90 min and report SI15-60 and SI15-90, with comparison to E1 and E5 local baselines. Measure a temperature sweep over 80-130 C as a secondary response and obtain at least duplicate, preferably triplicate, realizations.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Document exact masses, modifier identity and reactive-group specification, mixing history, reaction temperature/time, sample age, and preconditioning. Use a 120 C state-specific viscosity anchor for each realization, with matched E2 or local reference material when feasible, to calibrate viscosity scale; do not use that anchor as a substitute for the hold measurement.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: Thermal hold at 120 C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min; report both 15-60 min and 15-90 min SI.

evidence_against: No local modified-formulation hold data establish that either axis will reduce drift.
The acrylic evidence is chemically and process-wise noncommensurate with AC1920; external stability comparisons do not prove a local mechanism.
Major process-history fields are missing from the candidate definition, and E2 realization variability is high.
evidence_for: Full intervention coverage: includes both independently supported acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes.
Uses the E2 reactive-core proportions, preserving the locally characterized reactive core while adding 15 wt% AC1920-like modifier and 5 wt% TK100-like modifier.
The 5 wt% tackifier level is directly commensurate with the repeated external minor-resin cluster; the 15 wt% acrylic level is a directional lower-region anchor rather than an exact optimum.
Lowest total modifier burden among the strongly supported full-coverage candidates that retains a tackifier level in the directly supported minor-resin region.
Directly interrogates the hold-drift objective rather than optimizing distance to a literature composition.
key_uncertainty: Whether the combined 15/5 modifier loading reduces both short and extended hold drift after matched state control.
Whether any apparent improvement reflects altered initial viscosity or process state rather than improved stability.
Whether AC1920 functionality and TK100 reactive-group content are compatible with the assumed E2 stoichiometry.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This is the minimum-sufficient full-coverage performance test: it retains both independently supported intervention axes, stays near the characterized E2 chemistry, uses a directly supported minor tackifier level, and tests the failure mode with a matched 120 C hold rather than relying on static viscosity.

evidence_against: Higher total modifier burden than S1C41 and therefore a larger departure from the characterized local chemistry.
External analogue numeric viscosities are not directly commensurate with the local system and are not used as predicted outcomes.
Process-state uncertainty and missing thermal/mixing history remain substantial.
evidence_for: Full intervention coverage with 17.5 wt% acrylic-like modifier and 5 wt% minor tackifier-like modifier.

Both axes lie within the externally supported broad regions; the tackifier level is directly commensurate with the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, while the acrylic level is closer to the directly commensurate approximately 19-20 wt% family than the lower-bound candidate.
Provides a higher-intervention robustness comparison against S1C41 while preserving the same E2 reactive-core proportions.
External comparative evidence supports testing acrylic functionality/loading as a possible stability direction, without claiming a molecular mechanism.
key_uncertainty: Whether the increased acrylic loading provides additional hold-stability margin or merely changes initial viscosity and processability.
Whether the candidate remains stable across realizations when the E2-scale state variation is controlled.
Whether the combined loading introduces compatibility or stoichiometric effects not represented in the candidate metadata.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It tests robustness of the same two-axis mitigation strategy at a somewhat stronger, externally better anchored acrylic level. It is a useful escalation only after or alongside the minimum-sufficient S1C41 test, not because it is closest to a literature percentage.

evidence_against: The 10 wt% acrylic level is below the broad externally supported acrylic region of approximately 15-25 wt% and has only moderate analogue support.
Its 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the repeated directly commensurate 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster.
A null result would be ambiguous between insufficient intervention and unfavorable process/realization state.
evidence_for: Full intervention coverage with the lowest total modifier burden among full-coverage candidates.
Preserves the E2 reactive core and tests whether a small combined intervention can affect the established hold-drift failure.
Useful as a boundary probe for the lower edge of the supported family, distinguishing a genuinely low-burden effect from a response requiring stronger modifier loading.
key_uncertainty: Whether the low loading is chemically sufficient to alter hold drift.
Whether any viscosity change can be distinguished from E2 realization noise.
Whether the lower burden improves processability without providing meaningful stability mitigation.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This is a mechanistically informative lower-bound full-coverage probe, not the default performance choice. It resolves whether mitigation begins at a small combined perturbation while remaining close to E2, but its weaker external support makes it less suitable than S1C41 as the sole performance candidate.

evidence_against: Zeros both independently supported intervention axes and therefore cannot test the full performance-mitigation strategy.
Reactive-core-only behavior is already represented by the local E2 family; it does not directly test the resin-modification hypothesis.
evidence_for: Directly remains within the measured local reactive-core chemistry.
Provides a no-intervention reference for separating modifier effects from process-state and realization effects.
key_uncertainty: Whether the control realization is comparable to the modified candidates.
Whether residual drift is caused by reactive-core chemistry or realization state.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: Use as a matched process and measurement control, not as the rank-1 mitigation experiment. It anchors interpretation of any candidate hold-stability change against unmodified E2-like material.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: thermal-hold drift is formulation-dependent and must be measured directly; static temperature-sweep viscosity is not a proxy for hold stability.
Measured local evidence: E2 is the reactive-core anchor at 50/50 PDP70/PPG2000 and NCO:OH=1.80, but its realization variability is high at 120 C (CV approximately 0.585; max/min approximately 3.57).
Measured local evidence: local temperature support is 80-130 C, with a comparatively reproducible rheological temperature-sensitivity descriptor after state calibration.

Derived physical/model rule: represent each candidate as formulation plus process/realization state; a 120 C state-specific anchor can calibrate viscosity scale, but does not replace a matched hold test.
External analogue evidence: acrylic-like modifier levels near 19-20 wt% and 25 wt% are directly commensurate coarse anchors; the approximately 15 wt% acrylic evidence is directional/noncommensurate.
External analogue evidence: tackifier-like resin examples cluster around 4.8-6.4 wt%; below-about-10 wt% is a conservative formulation boundary, not an optimum.
External comparative evidence: lower-OH acrylic analogues showed lower long-hold viscosity growth than higher-OH analogues, but this does not establish a molecular mechanism in the local system.
Conservative design principle: for performance_mitigation, cover both independently supported acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes before applying minimum sufficient intervention.
Unresolved uncertainty: modifier chemistry, process history, reactive-group density, and realization state may dominate the observed viscosity level and could alter hold stability.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 C while preserving a measurable, processable formulation and separating modifier effects from realization/process-state variability. The failure mode is established locally by E5 drift (SI15-60=0.515; SI15-90=0.931) versus E1 (0.095; 0.168).
unresolved_questions: Does the combined acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like intervention reduce both short- and long-window drift under matched process conditions?
Is S1C41 sufficient, or is the higher acrylic loading in S1C46 required for a reproducible stability margin?
Does the low-loading boundary probe S1C30 show a real onset of mitigation or only process-state noise?
Are AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group densities compatible with the E2 NCO:OH=1.80 balance, or must stoichiometry be recalculated from verified specifications?
What process and sample-age controls are required to reduce the E2-scale realization variability?
Can any stability difference be attributed to formulation axes without claiming an unmeasured molecular mechanism?

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Retains full dual-axis coverage and the directly supported 5 wt% tackifier level while increasing acrylic loading from 15 to 17.5 wt%; this improves evidence-region coverage at the cost of a modestly larger modifier burden and greater departure from E2.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The objective remains performance mitigation but the 15 wt% acrylic level is treated as insufficiently supported or too weak for a decisive first test.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Has stronger independent region support for both axes, but its 25 wt% total modifier burden is larger and risks confounding stability with viscosity, processability, or state changes.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: Both the approximately 20 wt% acrylic anchor and the approximately 5 wt% tackifier cluster must be represented in one full-coverage performance test.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Preserves full axis coverage with lower total modifier loading, but both modifier levels have weaker support and a null result would be difficult to distinguish from insufficient intervention.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The immediate goal is a lower-burden uncertainty probe for whether any combined intervention signal exists near the lower edge of the supported region.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner no-intervention control, but it does not test the evidence-supported resin-modification mitigation strategy and is unsuitable as the primary performance candidate.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The experiment intent were causal isolation of reactive-core or process-state effects rather than performance mitigation.

required_conditions: Verify AC1920 and TK100 identities, functionality, reactive-group densities, and mass basis; recalculate the true NCO:OH balance before ranking any modified candidate.
Predeclare a numerical processable initial-viscosity interval and a replicate-level acceptance rule with an effect-size margin relative to E5 and an explicit uncertainty treatment.
Use matched unmodified E2-like process controls with documented mixing history, thermal history, sample age, preconditioning, and realization identity.
Retain the 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min and the 80-130 C temperature sweep; use the state anchor only for scale calibration, not as evidence of hold stability.
Treat S1C46 as a stronger full-coverage performance probe rather than as an exact optimum, and do not claim axis-specific or molecular attribution from a combined intervention.
If stoichiometry or processability cannot be verified, abstain from promoting any modified candidate to a definitive performance experiment.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 covers both independently supported intervention axes and directly tests thermal-hold drift at 120 C over 15-60 and 15-90 min rather than relying on static viscosity.
Because the declared intent is performance_mitigation, full dual-axis coverage is appropriate; S1C41 does not promote a partial-coverage candidate on modifier-burden grounds alone.

robustness_checks.check: Robustness to removal of exact analogue-distance rewards
robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 remains within the broad supported acrylic and tackifier regions, but its 15 wt% acrylic level is only directional/noncommensurate. S1C46 provides a stronger acrylic-region test with only a modest additional modifier burden.

AC1920 and TK100 functionality and reactive-group densities are unspecified, so fixed E2-derived MDI/polyol amounts do not establish a valid stoichiometric formulation or interpretable modifier intervention.

The proposed 120 C hold, 15/60/90 min measurements, temperature sweep, and replicate plan address the failure mode, but no numerical processable-viscosity interval, effect-size margin, or replicate-level uncertainty rule is predeclared.
The rationale does not depend on one analogue-distance score, but it depends materially on unverified modifier stoichiometry and on assuming that a combined 15/5 intervention is sufficient.
The stoichiometric ambiguity and nonquantitative acceptance rule are serious enough to prevent acceptance of S1C41 as the final experiment without an uncertainty-resolution step.

counterfactual_failures: If the candidate's initial viscosity is matched to E2 but hold SI is unchanged, the proposal has no explicit quantitative rule for declaring failure beyond the vague improvement criterion.

If the observed viscosity shift is attributed to realization state rather than chemistry, the state-anchor plan calibrates scale but does not independently establish comparable hold-state trajectories.

The proposed design cannot answer whether acrylic-only, tackifier-only, or combined intervention has different value under the performance objective because only the combined candidate is ranked as the performance test.

The conclusion may change under the conservative interpretation that 15 wt% acrylic is noncommensurate and that 5 wt% tackifier evidence supports only the tackifier axis, but this sensitivity is not made a formal ranking condition.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis states that E2 NCO:OH=1.80 applies only to the original reactive core and that true stoichiometry must be recalculated if modifiers contribute reactive groups. S1C41 nevertheless uses fixed E2-derived MDI/polyol amounts while adding 15 wt% AC1920-like and 5 wt% TK100-like material.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed formulation is not fully stoichiometrically specified or interpretable because AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group densities are unknown.

critical_findings.evidence: The criterion requires SI15-60 and SI15-90 to be lower than E5 and the direction to be retained after accounting for realization spread, but defines no effect-size margin, uncertainty model, replicate-level decision rule, or numerical processable-viscosity range. E5 is represented by a single original run, whereas the candidate is expected to have duplicates or triplicates.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion is not sufficiently quantitative or predeclared for adjudication.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 is the lowest-burden strongly supported full-coverage candidate, but no local modified-formulation hold data establish that 15/5 loading is sufficient to reduce drift. A null result would remain ambiguous between inadequate intervention and process/state variability.
critical_findings.issue: The proposal overstates intervention sufficiency by calling S1C41 a minimum-sufficient performance test before sufficiency has been demonstrated.

critical_findings.evidence: The external tackifier comparison is confounded by other formulation variables, and acrylic evidence is noncommensurate with AC1920. The proposal appropriately avoids a mechanistic claim, but the combined candidate still tests an unverified interaction and cannot attribute any effect to either axis.
critical_findings.issue: Independent support for two axes does not provide independent evidence that their combination is beneficial or non-antagonistic.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 uses 15 wt% acrylic, while the directly commensurate acrylic anchors are approximately 19-20 wt% and 25 wt%; the 15 wt% evidence is explicitly retained only as directional/noncommensurate. This is acceptable for candidate generation but weak support for rank-1 performance selection.
critical_findings.issue: The candidate's acrylic level is partly literature-near rather than locally evidenced for the measured failure mode.

critical_findings.evidence: The plan uses a state-specific 120 C viscosity anchor, but the acceptance criterion only says the initial viscosity must remain within an undefined processable range. The state-aware model supports scale calibration, not inference of hold stability from viscosity.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed comparison may confound improved stability with altered initial viscosity or state despite acknowledging that risk.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C01 is described as a matched process and measurement control, yet all baseline candidates have six missing process-history fields and no explicit matched realization, sample-age, thermal-history, or replicate protocol is specified.
critical_findings.issue: The no-intervention control is useful but its role and implementation are under-specified.

interpretability_failures: Verified modifier functionality, reactive-group density, and stoichiometric recalculation are required before attributing a hold response to the intended modifier axes.
The processable initial-viscosity range is undefined, so improvement through an impractical viscosity shift cannot be adjudicated objectively.
The phrase 'direction retained after accounting for realization spread' lacks a prespecified statistical or replicate-level rule.
A combined two-axis response cannot distinguish acrylic, tackifier, interaction, or shared process-state effects.
A candidate null result would not establish that the mitigation concept failed because intervention sufficiency is untested.

leakage_check.detail: The payload states that validation formulation identity and hold results were excluded. The rationale is traceable to original E1/E5/E2 measurements, external analogue evidence, and explicitly labeled conservative design rules. No held-out outcome is apparent in the proposed ranking.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly treats thermal-hold drift as distinct from static viscosity, uses the 120 C in-support anchor, acknowledges E2 realization/state variability, preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions, and selects a full-coverage two-axis candidate for a performance-mitigation intent. However, the claimed minimum-sufficient status is not established prospectively, and the acrylic 15 wt% level is supported only directionally/noncommensurately.

required_corrections: Verify AC1920 and TK100 composition, functionality, reactive-group density, and mass basis; recalculate NCO:OH and document whether the E2 reactive core is truly preserved.
Predeclare a numerical processable initial-viscosity interval and a quantitative replicate-based acceptance rule, including an effect-size margin relative to E5 and an uncertainty treatment.
Use matched unmodified E2-like process controls and document mixing, thermal history, sample age, preconditioning, and realization identity for every candidate replicate.
Retain the 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min and the 80-130 C temperature sweep, but do not use the state anchor as evidence of hold stability.
Downgrade the phrase 'minimum-sufficient' to 'lowest-burden strongly supported full-coverage candidate' unless sufficiency is established experimentally.

Either add a prespecified uncertainty-resolution comparison, such as S1C30 or an axis-specific control, or explicitly state that the combined S1C41 result is a performance screen and cannot support axis attribution.
Reassess rank-1 status if the 15 wt% acrylic level is treated as directional only; do not use exact literature proximity as evidence of a local optimum.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the distinction between local measured evidence, external analogue evidence, and conservative design principles, and does not claim a molecular mechanism. The boundary is weakened by presenting S1C41 as minimum-sufficient and rank-1 without local evidence of intervention sufficiency, while stoichiometric and process-history uncertainty remains unresolved.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Required canonical bridge before candidate ranking. It will confirm the formulation-only versus state-aware structure, whether state calibration materially improves the master curve, the local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, and the specific measurement implications for selecting a hold-stability intervention.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself.
